target_customer: Independent and regional grocery stores that pay an annual subscription, and shoppers who use the app
problem: Shoppers wait in checkout lines and independent grocers lack affordable self checkout.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription of $19,800 per year per grocer plus a 2% transaction fee on shoppers that might be dropped
product_category: Mobile scan and pay self checkout

founders.name: Sahle Hashelit
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch give no background.

founders.name: Erick Lee
founders.background_notes: Listed as CTO on the YC page and TechCrunch.

competitors.name: AisleBuyer
competitors.what: Shopping app that let people skip lines and pay on their phones
competitors.traction_then: Acquired by Intuit in 2012 and folded into GoPayment

technical_complexity.rationale: A barcode scanning and payment app with a grocer dashboard is standard mobile engineering; point of sale and loss prevention integration were the harder parts.

defensibility.rationale: Anyone could build a scan and pay app and large chains were building their own; a grocer integration was the only switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large chains launched in house scan and go tools around 2016 and Amazon announced Amazon Go in December 2016, per trade press seen in search; none acquired Selfycart.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (August 2016) reported live customers at two Bay Area grocers, partnership talks with two more and a planned $2 to 3 million seed round.

branding.domain_note: selfycart.com now redirects to a domain broker page (checked 2026-11), so the domain is for sale.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand beyond launch coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Selfycart launched at Rainbow Grocery and one other San Francisco store in August 2016 and sought a $2 to 3 million seed. No evidence shows that round closed; the only funding data is a small convertible note around September 2016 from one database. It is listed Inactive with no public cause, so failure factors stay empty, though large chains and Amazon were moving into the same wedge.
notes: The September 2016 note rests on CB Insights alone, which reports about $120K raised over three rounds including YC; amount of the note itself is unknown. Crunchbase shows seed raised with no amount. A loot-drop.io page claims $5.0M burned and a 2019 end year, but it labels itself AI generated, so it is not used. Cause of inactivity not public.
